reason: Article 9 establishes the scope and definitions of the AI Act, including what constitutes an AI system. It does not contain any obligations related to monitoring.
Article 20 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to establish a post-market monitoring system. This directly supports the control objective of monitoring for drift, misuse, and emerging risks.
Article 26(5) pertains to the obligations of users of high-risk AI systems, specifically regarding human oversight. It does not address the provider's monitoring obligations.

Article 72 outlines the powers of the European Artificial Intelligence Board, which is an administrative and governance provision. It does not impose a direct monitoring obligation on providers or users.
